title: Tadla irrigated plain, Beni Moussa side, 4 Jul to 2 Sep 2026
summary: From 4 Jul to 2 Sep 2026 the radar shows 6.44 km2 turning brighter and 12.21 km2 darker in HV on the Tadla plain, inside the 9 km circle. Most of the darker area, 9.56 km2, is on the changing fields.

sections.heading: What changed
sections.text: Over 60 days mean HV moved by -0.12 dB and mean HH by 0.45 dB. In HV, 6.44 km2 turned brighter by more than 3 dB and 12.21 km2 darker; in HH, 12.98 km2 turned brighter and 10.22 km2 darker.

sections.heading: Where, by terrain type
sections.text: The changing fields had 4.32 km2 brighter and 9.56 km2 darker in HV, with a mean HV change of -1.24 dB. Rough dry ground and fields had 1.56 km2 brighter and 1.84 km2 darker in HV. Trees, shrub and rugged slopes changed by 0.07 dB in HV, and built-up land by 0.47 dB in HH.

sections.heading: Possible causes
sections.text: Possible cause for the darker fields: summer harvests, which remove the plants that scatter HV; harvest records from the irrigation office would confirm it. Possible cause for the brighter fields: crops sown or growing on other plots; a field visit would check it. Possible cause for part of the HH rise, built-up land included: a small calibration difference between the acquisitions; stable targets on more dates would check it.

sections.heading: Limits
sections.text: Neither date carries a flag. NASA has no NISAR data from 27 Jul to 10 Aug 2026, so nothing between 16 Jul and 21 Aug 2026 is seen. One track only, so field edges facing away from the radar can look darker.

sections.heading: What an agency could do next
sections.text: An irrigation office could compare the 9.56 km2 of darker fields with its harvest and water-delivery records. An insurer could use the dated change to confirm when a parcel was harvested.
